question.text: A long straight wire carrying a current of <math><mn>30</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> is placed in an external uniform magnetic field of induction <math><mn>4</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math> . The direction of external magnetic field is along the direction of the current. The magnitude of the resultant magnetic induction at a point <math><mn>2.0</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> away from the wire is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math>. What is the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math>?

solution.text:
Magnetic field due to wire

B=μ0I2πr=4π×10-72π×302×10-2

=3×10-4 T

This magnetic field will be perpendicular to external magnetic field.

∴ Net magnetic field

B=B2+B02

=3× 10–4 2+4×10–4 2

=5×10–4 T
